explain.say: The core of the Burj Khalifa in Dubai rose inside self-climbing formwork, a moulding machine that jacked itself up about a floor every few days. Formwork is the temporary mould wet concrete is poured into; falsework is the scaffolding that holds it up. On the board, the forces on one face of a wall mould.

explain.say: Wet concrete behaves like a heavy liquid. Its pressure grows with depth, twenty five kilopascals for every metre, because concrete weighs about twenty five kilonewtons per cubic metre. Look at the line: pour a wall three metres deep in one go and the bottom of the mould feels seventy five kilopascals. How would pouring more slowly help?

explain.say: The lower concrete starts to stiffen, so the pressure stops growing! Steel tie rods through the wall hold the two faces together. Look at the tie: if ties sit every six hundred millimetres each way, each one holds back zero point three six square metres at seventy five kilopascals, twenty seven kilonewtons. Raking props keep the panel upright.

draw.text: Tie load = 75 kPa × 0.6 m × 0.6 m = 27 kN

explain.say: Now a slab. A two hundred millimetre slab weighs five kilopascals; add half a kilopascal of formwork and one and a half for workers and kit: seven. With props on a one point two metre grid, each prop holds ten kilonewtons, about a tonne. Look at the arrows: what happens if one prop is knocked out?

explain.say: Its load jumps onto its neighbours, and falsework collapses have killed workers, so props are checked by a temporary works engineer. Forms stay until the concrete is strong enough. Look at the groups: wall sides after about a day, but slab props one to two weeks. Superb! Challenge: what pressure does a four metre wall pour put on the bottom of its form?

faq.q: What is the difference between formwork and falsework?
faq.a: Formwork is the mould that gives concrete its shape: panels, shutters and their ties. Falsework is the temporary structure, such as props and scaffolds, that supports formwork and wet concrete until it can carry itself.

faq.q: How do you calculate concrete pressure on formwork?
faq.a: For full liquid head, pressure equals the concrete unit weight, about 25 kilonewtons per cubic metre, times the depth. A 3 metre pour gives 75 kilopascals; slow pours and setting can reduce it.
asks: How do you calculate concrete pressure on formwork?

faq.a: Ties are steel rods or bolts through the wall that hold the two faces of the formwork together against the concrete pressure. Each carries the pressure on its share of panel area.

faq.q: How much load does a slab prop carry?
faq.a: The slab self-weight plus formwork plus construction load, times the area each prop supports. Seven kilopascals on a 1.2 by 1.2 metre grid gives about 10 kilonewtons per prop.
When the concrete is strong enough. India's IS 456 suggests 16 to 24 hours for vertical faces, 3 days for slab soffits with props refixed, and 7 to 21 days for props depending on span.

facts: Fresh normal-weight concrete weighs about 24 to 25 kN/m³.
IS 456 gives 7 days for props to slabs spanning up to 4.5 m and 14 days for longer spans.
